headline: Army detonates Iowa explosives, calls it a success
pages: The US Army on Wednesday detonated nearly five tonnes of lead azide, a toxic and volatile explosive, at a site in Iowa. Smoke rose shortly after 9 a.m. local time. The Army said the risk was as close to zero as humanly possible and called the operation a huge success. The plan had been paused several times after public outcry and legal challenges. The explosives had been stored for about 20 years and had degraded in a way that made them easier to set off by friction or movement. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said EPA sensors in the area showed no readings above zero. President Donald Trump said mitigation efforts far exceeded expectations.

Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson said he felt relieved and vindicated, and residents several miles away said they felt and saw nothing. Officials have called early lead readings promising, though no level of lead exposure is considered safe, especially for children and pregnant women. More sampling is expected. Source: BBC News.
